Corollary
[Covering Map Homeomorphism Criterion] ↗ thm:lifting-criterion 1. chA:A.58

A covering map $\pi : \tilde{M} \to M$ is a homeomorphism if and only if the induced homomorphism $\pi _*: \pi _1(\tilde{M}, \tilde{x}) \to \pi _1(M, \pi (\tilde{x}))$ is surjective for some (hence every) $\tilde{x} \in \tilde{M}$. A smooth covering map is a diffeomorphism if and only if the induced homomorphism is surjective.

Proof. By Theorem A.56, the hypothesis implies that the identity map $\operatorname {Id}: M \to M$ has a lift $\widetilde{\operatorname {Id}}: \tilde{M} \to \tilde{M}$, which in this case is a continuous inverse for $\pi $. If $\pi $ is a smooth covering map, then the lift is also smooth. $\square $
